=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:892-893 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When cached review_only evidence is rejected, collect_run returns {"skipped": True} without deleting the run_dir directory from disk.
  WHY: A previous collect that built evidence for a failed run writes meta.json and job log files. A subsequent collect that sees the same run as review_only (e.g. the run concluded success with non-review jobs mixed in) rejects the cached evidence at lines 892-893 but leaves meta.json and orphaned job log files on disk. In production each workflow stage has its own evidence directory, so the stale files do not cross stages, but within-stage re-collection by the same Collector would encounter stale evidence.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:881-893 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When the cached review-only evidence is rejected by the new guard at lines 884-891, the function returns {"skipped": True} without removing the previously cached runs/<repo>__<run_id> directory.
  WHY: The four tests `test_review_only_run_does_not_trust_malformed_cached_job_table`, `test_review_only_run_rejects_empty_cached_review_jobs`, `test_review_only_run_rejects_cached_non_review_log_even_with_review_job`, and `test_review_only_run_rejects_orphaned_cached_non_review_log` all assert `not run_dir.exists()` immediately after the cached rejection, but the code does not remove `run_dir` from `self.out`. The cached `meta.json` + leftover `job-*.txt` files also survive into the next stage through `actions/cache`, so a subsequent stage receives the same untrusted evidence the guard was meant to discard and burns a budget retry on a head that can never be re-collected.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:142 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_HEAL_RUN_LINE_RE` is defined with a "retained for compatibility" comment but `trusted_run_refs` no longer references it (it switched to `_runs_marker_urls(...)` on lines 574 and 614 in this PR). No other module imports it; the only match in the tree is the definition itself.
  WHY: dead code — no runtime failure today — but future maintainers will trace a usage that does not exist, and the comment implies an external consumer that the diff did not preserve. Per §6, the safest minimal fix is to delete the symbol (or move it next to a real caller).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:905-907 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the fresh path encounters a `review_only` run whose job list contains zero matching focus jobs (e.g. `test_review_only_run_with_only_failed_non_review_job_skips_evidence`), it returns without cleaning the run directory either.
  WHY: the pre-existing `runs/<repo>__<run_id>/` dir from a prior non-`review_only` stage (or an earlier, different conclusion) stays on disk with stale `job-*.txt` files for jobs the review-only guard rejected. The next stage restores the same dir through `actions/cache` and the untrusted non-review logs survive into the trusted evidence folder.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
